Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rishi (applied ML infra) and Lauren (account lead) so we can provide both the high-level attestation and the technical artifacts.

Short answers up front:
- Tenant data isolation: Dedicated pools are allocated as tenant-bound GPU nodes with OS-level namespace isolation, per-tenant ephemeral volumes with full-disk encryption, and strict KV cache scoping so that in-memory KV cache (modelKV) is not shared across tenants. We do not allow co-mingled model state on the same process for dedicated allocations.
- Noisy neighbor / contention mitigation: Our runtime enforces request-level QoS via a combination of continuous batching limits per tenant, soft/hard eviction thresholds based on GPU memory pressure and per-tenant token-throttle budgets, and scheduler-level fairness (weighted round-robin with tenant weight caps).
- Attestation: We can provide a signed attestation stating that Dedicated Capacity is tenant-bound and that we do not co-host multiple tenants' inference state in the same serving process for dedicated nodes.

I've attached a trimmed architecture diagram and will ask Rishi to follow up with more detail and the eviction policy text. If you can share which SIG rows are highest priority in the workbook, we'll triage those first.

1) Rishi to send a concise technical addendum (eviction signals, metrics names) — targeted follow-up within 24 hours.
2) Lauren to coordinate the attestation and get the DocuSign link if a signature is required.
3) I'll provide the architecture diagram and a redacted telemetry sample if security allows.

Emma / team — technical addendum below. Quoted for context.

On Thu, Jun 18, 2026 at 09:12 AM Emma Dyson <emma.dyson@cloudcorp.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the SIG responses you submitted last week. Our Security & Risk team reviewed your answers and has a couple of follow-up asks specifically around Dedicated GPU instances and multi-tenant contention risk.
> 
> Topline questions:
> - Can you confirm how you guarantee tenant data isolation on shared GPU hosts (kernel/user memory separation, KV cache isolation, ephemeral disk encryption)?
> - How do you mitigate noisy-neighbor GPU contention (runtime throttling, eviction, QoS policies)? Particularly: what eviction thresholds, observable signals, and tenant-level metrics are used?
> - Do you have an attestation or signed letter that states Dedicated capacity provides tenant isolation for our contract?

Technical addendum (concise):
1) Process & memory isolation:
- Dedicated capacity uses tenant-assigned VM/GPU nodes (no mix of tenant workloads on the same host for 'dedicated' SKUs). Each tenant's inference processes run in separate containers on that node. We rely on the OS + container runtime for kernel/user memory separation; we do not map customer data into other tenants' processes.
- Persistent storage is tenant-scoped: ephemeral disks are encrypted with per-tenant KMS keys; snapshots are disabled for dedicated nodes by default.

2) KV cache and model state:
- The runtime maintains a per-request KV cache in process memory. For dedicated nodes we guarantee that the KV cache instance belongs to a single tenant process. There is no cross-tenant shared KV cache for dedicated pools.

3) Contention detection signals & eviction policy:
- Signals we observe: GPU memory utilization by process, GPU SM occupancy percent, CUDA OOM events, per-tenant token-generation latency percentiles (p50/p95), and host-level GPU temperature spikes.
- Eviction flow (summary):
  * Soft signal: sustained p95 latency > service SLO for 30s or GPU memory growth rate above threshold. We start applying per-tenant token-throttles (reduce concurrent generation streams).
  * Hard signal: CUDA OOM or sustained >95% GPU memory utilization for >10s triggers eviction of lower-priority jobs on the node. Eviction selects tasks by policy (preemptible flag, tenant priority, and time-in-queue) and migrates them to the node's eviction queue for restart on other capacity.
  * We keep an event audit trail for evictions (tenant id, task id, reason code, timestamp).

4) Scheduling & QoS:
- Scheduler uses weighted tenant caps and continuous batching caps to limit concurrent memory footprint per tenant. We enforce limits at the runtime layer before batching to prevent a single tenant from monopolizing tensor memory.
- For workloads that require strict isolation, customers can opt for single-tenant pinned nodes (no eviction) as part of an enterprise Dedicated SLA.

5) Observability / evidence we can share:
- Eviction logs (redacted): timestamps, reason codes, tenant priority.
- Per-tenant p95 latency histograms over a 7-day window (anonymized).
- Architecture diagram and policy text (attached).

6) Compliance caveat:
- While Dedicated pools are tenant-bound, we still perform kernel and driver updates via scheduled maintenance windows. We maintain change logs and can provide patch history for nodes in scope under an NDA.

If you want example metric names for ingestion: redwood.serving.<pool>.tenant.<tenant_id>.latency.p95, redwood.serving.<pool>.tenant.<tenant_id>.gpu.mem_pct, redwood.serving.<pool>.tenant.<tenant_id>.eviction.count.

Attachment: eviction-policy.txt (text/plain, 3.4KB)
